newsitem.title: FRANCE: Colour is back with a vengeance on Paris catwalk.
newsitem.headline: Colour is back with a vengeance on Paris catwalk.

text.p: - Forever true to his flamboyant instincts, Christian Lacroix unleashed a collage of African, Indian and 18th-century French inspiration on Thursday in his new ready-to-wear collection.

Lacroix's world is one of vivid ethnic and historical references -- lace-up bustiers on checkered kneepants, Marquis jackets with jewelled buttons, swelling Masai princess skirts or bou-bous that hung amply from a band above the chest.
Each oufit was a wild patchwork, juxtaposing macrame, beads, gold embroidery and bits of lace and luscious shantung.
"It's everything from Africa to India, but mixed and matched in a way that's for the next millennium," was how Lacroix defined it. "A city-dweller's exoticism," he added.

Lacroix, whose sales doubled last year, has reason to hope he will finally turn a profit and placate his boss, Bernard Arnault, chairman of luxury goods giant LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton, when his house turns 10 next year.
All eyes this season are on LVMH which is expected to announce next Tuesday the appointment of Britain's maverick romantic John Galliano as the new designer for Christian Dior.

Another Briton, the irreverent Alexander McQueen, is tipped for the position Galliano would be leaving vacant at LVMH sister house Givenchy. A brief appearance by McQueen at Lacroix's show was a strong indication he would be Givenchy's new man.
"I really enjoyed it, it's a totally different concept from what I'm all about, but the colours are fantastic," he said.
Asked whether he had decided to accept the Givenchy job, McQueen replied: "I'm afraid you'll have to wait for that."
Sonia Rykiel celebrated her 6,000th sweater design, offering a knitwear restrospective that spanned the colour spectrum.

The veteran designer, who is also known as the "Queen of Knitwear", then unfurled next summer's knits -- middy tube dresses of multi-coloured stripes, leopard spots on tank tops and skimpy camisoles over bikini bottoms, lurex draw-string trousers and fishnet tops over tiny shorts which sent the photographers roaring with delight.

Finally, Rykiel moved on to cotton: striped or plaid jumpsuits, a few magenta crepe trousers suits and jeans with drawstring flies. For evening there were transparent lace gowns with panties underneath.
It was an upbeat, colourful affair, featuring more than 60 models. And although there was not a novelty in sight, Rykiel does deserve her title.
Lolita Lempicka, the queen of separates, sent out bright florals on black, snakeskin chiffons, and vivid colour combinations -- fuchsia with orange, magenta with turquoise, yellow with lime.

It was all that trendy teenagers have been wearing on the streets: stretchy flared trousers, viscose knit twinsets and a series of ensembles in chartreuse and flame, the hottest shades from last season's catwalk.

On just the fourth day of the ready-to-wear season, which continues until the beginning of next week, clear trends are emerging. Knits, nudity, transparence and short and midriff sets have come up on several catwalks, with a broad range of purples as the dominant palette.
